To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

• The majority of general practices do not have a fail-safe system for checking that all results are returned from laboratories and that results are communicated to patients; • Patients are responsible for ensuring that results are retrieved and practices rely on patients to report missing or delayed results; • The majority of practices do not use electronic result communication systems and there appears to be a reluctance to adopt these systems.

1) the current process for communicating test results in primary care relies on the patient to request their results and is vulnerable to error; and 2) practices are slow to adopt technological solutions that could reduce error and improve efficiency.
the majority of practices in our study used the telephone to communicate test results and that this system was vulnerable to human error and failure.
